result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_selected_node_ids()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get currently selected node IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11908-L11961){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_selected_node_ids() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Get selected node ids](/assets/graphs/get-selected-node-ids.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Six nodes labeled by their integer ids 1 to 6, with nodes 2, 4, and 6 selected in the accent color. get_selected_node_ids() returns the list of those ids, 6, 4, 2, in no guaranteed order." width="100%"} Returns the IDs of the nodes that are currently in the node selection, as built up by the `select_*`, `deselect_*`, `invert_*`, and `trav_*` methods. It is a read-only view: calling it does not change the selection. Use it to inspect what a selection rule actually matched, to pass the selected nodes to a method that takes explicit node IDs (such as `subgraph()`), or to save a selection and restore it later with `select_nodes_by_id()`. The selection is stored as a set, so the order of the returned IDs is arbitrary and may differ between runs; sort the list if you need a stable order. If you only need to know how many nodes are selected, `count_selected_nodes()` avoids building the list. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of selected node IDs in no particular order, empty if no nodes are selected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a 5-node star, only the hub has degree `3` or higher, so it's the only node selected: ::: {#9cfb6ae1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(5) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3) ) graph.get_selected_node_ids() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1] ``` ::: ::: IDs are integers, so map them to labels to make the result readable, sorting first for a stable order. Here the nodes with a score above `5` are "B" and "D": ::: {#0a2c7c9e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes({"A": {"score": 2}, "B": {"score": 8}, "C": {"score": 4}, "D": {"score": 7}}) .select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes["score"] > 5) ) [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in sorted(graph.get_selected_node_ids())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['B', 'D'] ``` ::: :::
